I suspect the Gabe Steam circlejerk started from astroterfing. Enough brand loyalty and a company can get away with anything. I like how it didn't work with the mod shop.

I suspect you may not have had the pleasure of gaming on PC much before Steam. Before Steam PC gaming was a nightmare. Companies were going psychotic with DRM with all sorts of fun things that were at times going to the point of physically damaging computer hardware - Starforce DRM for instance fried my disc drive. Updating games was a nightmare. You basically had to seek out the publisher's random page, if it still existed for your game and pray the links were still valid as they were often hosted off-site. Multiplayer was no better with games often relying on random third party services which you'd also have to sign up for (like Gamespy) and it was a complete pain in the ass. And then actually buying games? Don't even get me started...

That's from a gamer perspective. From a developer perspective it was even worse. Getting any visibility was all but impossible without a publisher. And getting a publisher often meant excessive schmoozing just to get a shot at pitching your game. And if after all of this work you finally did get through and managed to hit a contract you'd be looking at something like 15% of the profits from your game, and that'd be after the publisher deducted 100% of their costs from the gross. And don't even think about selling it elsewhere. In fact there's a good chance you'd actually have to sign off all rights to the game as well. Steam gives developer's about 70% of total gross for every single sale with no obligation allowing developers to sell or port the game to whatever other platforms they like and even sell Steam Keys for their game while completely cutting out Valve.

Steam was pretty bad at first acting like little more than yet another DRM and matchmaking service primarily for Valve's own games, but it rapidly blossomed into something amazing and they've generally tended to do everything they can make things right every single time there's been a meaningful problem. Gabe could have long since gone public with the company, cashed out likely to the tune of billions, and let some monkey suits come destroy the company in a fit of profiteering but he hasn't. The reason it might seem impersonal is because they have more than 125,000,000 active users, 4500 games, and 400 million piece of use generated content available. If just 1% of their userbase has a problem each month, that's more than a million problems more than 30,000 per day or a thousand an hour. All in all Steam has completely revolutionized PC gaming.
